Care of Challenged Children

Care of challenged children — disability types, rehabilitation, family support, special education, adoption and legal protection.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe types of disability in children
  • Explain the rehabilitation process
  • Support the family of a challenged child
  • Describe school inclusion and legal protection

In simple words

“Challenged child” is a child with a physical, sensory, intellectual or developmental disability that makes ordinary activity harder. Care aims at maximum ability and inclusion, not a cure label.

Types of challenges

Type Example
Physical Cerebral palsy, polio, spina bifida, limb deficiency, amputations
Sensory Blindness and low vision, deafness and hardness of hearing
Intellectual Intellectual impairment, down syndrome, learning disability
Developmental Autism, speech delay, cerebral palsy
Chronic illness Thalassaemia, renal failure, congenital heart disease requiring long-term care
Behavioural and emotional ADHD, severe anxiety, conduct problems

Rehabilitation

  • Medical — treat complications, epilepsy, contractures and pain
  • Physical — physiotherapy, occupational therapy, orthoses, prostheses
  • Communication — speech therapy, sign language, hearing aids
  • Psychosocial — counselling, play therapy, vocational training
  • Educational — special education and inclusive schools
  • Community-based — home training and parent groups

Law and rights

  • Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 — 21 disabilities, reservations in education, employment and accessibility
  • National Trust Act — guardianship and welfare of persons with autism, cerebral palsy and mental retardation
  • Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and inclusive education
  • Adoption is permitted for couples under the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 and the Juvenile Justice Act

🔴 Ability first, disability second

Describe and treat the whole child. Assess what the child can do and build from there. Never let a physical disability be a reason for missing school, immunisation or play.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. RBSK screens children for defects and developmental delay.
  2. Aims of care are functional ability and inclusion, not cure.
  3. Rehabilitation is medical, physical, communication, psychosocial and educational.
  4. RPwD Act, 2016 gives rights and reservations in education and jobs.
  5. Parent groups and home training support long-term care.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Early intervention improves outcome for cerebral palsy and autism.
  2. School inclusion reduces stigma and improves participation.
  3. Family counselling prevents breakdown of care.
  4. Adoption has legal requirements and courts.
  5. Chronic illness needs education, vocation and psychosocial support.

📌 Memory trick

Care of challenged children: A-R-S-I — Assess early, Rehabilitate, Support the family, Include.

60-second revision

  • Types of challenges: physical, sensory, intellectual, developmental, chronic.
  • Rehabilitation: medical, physical, communication, psychosocial, education.
  • Family support, home training and respite.
  • Inclusive education under RPwD Act, 2016.
  • Assess ability, set realistic goals, promote independence.

Test yourself

Early screening for disability in children in India is provided by:

Answer: B. RBSK screens children for birth defects, deficiency, diseases and developmental delay.

The aims of rehabilitation are:

Answer: B. Rehabilitation aims at maximum functional ability and inclusion in family, school and community.

The main law protecting disabled persons in India is:

Answer: B. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 gives rights, reservations and accessibility.

Which support is most important for the family of a challenged child?

Answer: B. Family counselling, realistic goal-setting and home training maintain long-term care.

A child with cerebral palsy should be:

Answer: B. Early physiotherapy, aids and inclusion in school maximise function and participation.
